node_types.description: Fade up while the gate is on and fade down when it lets go: rises to 1 over `attack_seconds`, falls to 0 over `release_seconds`.
Smooth a jumpy number: follow it, taking about `seconds` to catch up.
A smooth wave that swings between -1 and 1, rate_hz times a second. Wire it into any number input to animate it.
On and off in a steady beat: on for the first `width` of each cycle, rate_hz times a second. Set rate_hz to BPM / 60 for a beat.
A number that climbs from 0 to 1 and starts over, rate_hz times a second. Drives anything that loops: a wipe, a rotation, a scroll.
Turn a speed into a position: adds `rate` every second, so a steady input makes a steadily growing number. Reset sends it back to 0.
Seconds since the stream started, or since reset was last on.
Recolour a picture with two colours: one for the shadows, one for the highlights.
Shift hue around the colour wheel (0 to 1 is one full turn) and scale saturation and brightness.
Flip every colour to its opposite, like a film negative. Amount fades the effect in.
Brightness, contrast, gamma and opacity in one node. Brightness adds, contrast multiplies around mid grey.
Recolour a picture through a gradient: dark pixels take the gradient's left edge, bright ones its right.
Turn a picture black and white. Amount fades between colour and grey.
Reduce a picture to a few flat colour steps per channel, for a screen-print look.
Pure black below a brightness, pure white above it. Softness blurs the cut.
Multiply a picture by a colour, like a coloured gel over a light.
Add b's light onto a. Black adds nothing, so it suits glows, sparks and projections.
Show where two pictures differ: black where they match, bright where they do not.
Darken a by b. White changes nothing, so it suits shadows and textures.
Lighten a by b, more gently than Blend Add and never past white.
Cut a picture to a shape: it stays where the mask is white and turns see-through where the mask is black.
Crossfade between two pictures: all of a at 0, all of b at 1.
Lay a foreground over a background, showing the background wherever the foreground is see-through.
Slide from picture a to picture b along a moving edge. Angle is in turns; softness feathers the edge.
Soften a picture. Radius is a fraction of its height: 0.01 is gentle, 0.05 is heavy. Chain two for a smoother blur.
Make one colour see-through, such as a green screen. Layer the result over a background with Over.
Bend a picture using another one as a map: the map's red pushes pixels sideways, its green up and down. Try Noise as the map.
Draw only the outlines in a picture: white lines where brightness changes, black elsewhere.
Make the dark parts of a picture see-through, keeping the bright parts.
Turn a picture into big square blocks. Fewer cells across means bigger blocks.
Pull the red and blue apart for a glitchy, out-of-register look. Angle is in turns: 0.25 is straight up.
Crisp up edges and fine detail.
Darken the corners of a picture to draw the eye to the middle.
Black and white squares, for lining up a projector or testing an effect.
A filled circle on a see-through background. Use it as a spotlight, a dot, or a mask.
A smooth fade from one colour to another across the frame. Angle is in turns: 0 runs left to right, 0.25 top to bottom.
Soft grey clouds. Wire a Timer or a Speed into time to make them drift. A good map for Displace and a good mask.
A round fade from an inner colour at the centre to an outer colour at the radius.
A filled rectangle on a see-through background. Width and height are fractions of the frame.
Evenly spaced bars at any angle. Wire a Ramp into scroll to make them march.
Show a picture from the project's assets. Pick a PNG or JPEG you imported in its `asset` setting.
Whether a is less than, equal to or greater than b.
Count how many times its input has turned on.
Let a signal of any kind through while open, and block it while closed.
Freeze a picture: hold the first frame until refresh takes a newer one.
Grab a number when sample turns on and hold it until the next time.
Pick one of four numbers by index.
Pick one of two numbers with an on/off input.
A one-frame pulse each time its input turns on.
Drop a number's sign.
Add two numbers.
Hold a number between a low and a high limit.
A number you set once and wire to many inputs.
Divide a by b. Gives 0 when b is 0.
Blend between two numbers: a at t = 0, b at t = 1.
The larger of two numbers.
The smaller of two numbers.
The remainder after dividing a by b. Wraps a rising number into a repeating range.
Multiply two numbers.
Smooth wandering noise between -1 and 1. Wire a Timer into x to make it drift.
Raise a number to a power.
A new random number every frame, between low and high.
Rescale a number from one range to another. By default -1..1 becomes 0..1, which fits an LFO to a 0..1 input.
Ease from 0 to 1 as a number crosses from one edge to the other.
0 below an edge, 1 at or above it.
Subtract b from a.
A steady tone: a sine, square, saw or triangle wave at the pitch you set. Wire it into Program, or to a Speaker, to hear it.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The tone, the same on every channel

node_types.description: A flat colour at the size you set, sent about 60 times a second. Also the blank canvas a generator such as Noise or Gradient takes its size and its frame rate from.
Cut away the edges of a picture, each by a fraction of the frame. What is cut is see-through.
Mirror a picture left to right, top to bottom, or both. Set each to 1 to flip.
Fold a picture into mirrored wedges around its centre. Wire a Ramp into rotate to make it spin.
Reflect one half of a picture onto the other, for a symmetric image.
Repeat a picture in a grid. Wire a Ramp into scroll to slide the tiles forever.
Move, resize and turn a picture. Move is a fraction of the frame, scale 1 is full size, rotate is in turns (0.25 is a quarter turn). Outside the picture is see-through.
Layers up to eight video inputs back to front, in premultiplied alpha, on the GPU

inputs.name: layer_0
inputs.description: The backmost layer; each frame yields one composite

inputs.name: layer_1
inputs.description: Layered over layer_0; its newest frame is held

inputs.name: layer_2
inputs.description: Layered over layer_1; its newest frame is held

inputs.name: layer_3
inputs.description: Layered over layer_2; its newest frame is held

inputs.name: layer_4
inputs.description: Layered over layer_3; its newest frame is held

inputs.name: layer_5
inputs.description: Layered over layer_4; its newest frame is held

inputs.name: layer_6
inputs.description: Layered over layer_5; its newest frame is held

inputs.name: layer_7
inputs.description: The frontmost layer; its newest frame is held

outputs.name: video
outputs.description: The composite, premultiplied RGBA at the configured canvas size

node_types.description: A number as it was at the last evaluation. A loop of number nodes closes through it.
